name: NX2navi
readmeHtml:
NX2navi

Important

NX2navi is no longer the current project. NX2navi and Triforce have merged and go on as Triforce. Get Triforce from https://triforceproject.com. Its source is at https://git.triforceproject.com/triforce/source.

This repository and its releases are kept as they are. Release 0.12.0 turns an installed NX2navi launcher into a window that starts Triforce Setup; Play NX2navi there still starts the game you have built, and your game, saves and settings stay where they are. Triforce's Convert saves page brings your NX2navi saves over.

Join the official Triforce update discord server: https://discord.com/invite/uf6gSrsPpq

NX2navi is a static recompilation of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 (game version 1.1.1) into a native x86-64 application for Windows, with a Vulkan renderer (docs/architecture.md).

Important

No game files are included. You need your own legally obtained copy of the game, dumped from your own console. Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided.

The game is built from your files on your machine, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use. Do not share it.

Status

New work goes into Triforce, not here (see the top of this page). What follows describes NX2navi as it was at the handover.

Playable. Kokiri Forest, Kakariko Village, Death Mountain Trail and its crater, the Temple of Time and the Great Fairy fountains play at 60 fps and above on current GPUs, from the title screen and from saves. Visual bugs and occasional crashes are still expected (Known issues).

Report problems as issues, following CONTRIBUTING.md.

Features

  • Native code, not emulation
  • 60 fps by default, or a limit of 30 to 240 fps, the display's refresh rate or unlimited
  • Native widescreen and ultrawide (the window's shape, 21:9 or 32:9) with the HUD, menus and movies kept 16:9
  • Game resolutions from 1080p to above the game's 1440p: 1800p, 4K, 5K or the window's own size, sharp on high-DPI displays
  • Upscaling and anti-aliasing: NVIDIA DLSS (DLAA, Quality, Balanced, Performance, Ultra Performance; RTX GPUs) or AMD FSR 3.1 (Native AA and the same modes; any GPU) or AMD FSR 4 (the same modes; Radeon RX 6000, RX 7000 and RX 9000 GPUs), which render the 3D scene at the mode's share and keep the HUD sharp; or AMD FSR 1 or bilinear scaling to the window, with a sharpness setting; black bars or stretch
  • Frame generation: NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation (RTX 40 and 50 GPUs, paced with Reflex) at 2x, or 3x and 4x on RTX 50 GPUs (one, two or three generated frames for every frame the game draws), or AMD FSR 3.1 (any GPU), a generated frame between every two the game draws, with the HUD kept out of it, for about twice the frame rate on a fast display; in a window of another shape than the picture, frames are generated inside the picture only, so the black bars stay clean. The frame limit counts the frames the game draws, and frame generation adds its frames on top of it. The frame limit can also be handed to RivaTuner Statistics Server, which then limits the game in its place once it is seen holding the game; the game paces movies itself, and takes the limit back while it is minimised and whenever RivaTuner is not seen holding it; where frame generation or low latency keeps it out, the game says when a limit set in RivaTuner itself holds the game as well
  • HDR on HDR displays, two kinds: the game's scene tone mapped to the display's peak, matched to the game's mid grey and tone, with true blacks, or the game's own native HDR; peak, game and HUD brightness in the menu, and for the tone mapped picture the tone mapper, gamma correction, exposure, highlights, shadows, contrast and saturation
  • The game's known shaders prepared when the game is built, and the pipelines met in play built again in the background at each start, so play rarely stops to compile them; a shader or pipeline met for the first time can still hold a frame, and a draw that must wait for its pipeline has it built on worker threads, never on the game's drawing thread
  • In-game settings menu (F1, or Minus and Plus together on a gamepad) and performance overlay (F10)
  • Keyboard, mouse and gamepads with remapping, Nintendo, Xbox or PlayStation button layout, rumble and gyro; the game follows whichever connected gamepad you press, and DualShock 3 controllers are read directly when enabled
  • Xbox, PlayStation, Steam Deck and keyboard and mouse button prompts in the game's own text, drawn on your PC when the game is built; the keyboard prompts follow your key bindings
  • Stereo or 5.1 surround sound output, on the output device of your choice; the default microphone for the game's microphone input
  • The monitor the game opens on, straight in fullscreen when fullscreen is on
  • Your Discord status shows "Playing NX2navi" with the play time (on by default; the Game tab of the menu or the launcher's Settings turns it off)
  • Docked or handheld console mode
  • The game's textures stay compressed (BC3, about half the video memory at the same speed) unless the PC has 20 GiB of video memory and 48 GiB of RAM, as Windows counts video memory against the system's commit limit

Installing

New here: get Triforce from https://triforceproject.com instead. Release 0.12.0 carries no setup, and a launcher installed from an earlier release updates itself into the window that starts Triforce Setup. The rest of this section describes NX2navi's own setup before 0.12.0.

Download NX2navi-Setup-<version>.exe from the releases and start it next to your .nup dump. It is the only file you need. The launcher it installs finds the dump, downloads the build tools, builds the game on your PC (20 to 45 minutes, once) and starts it; afterwards it keeps the port up to date and rebuilds only what changed (docs/launcher.md). docs/README-BuildKit.md describes the same build by hand, docs/building.md building from source. Settings are in the in-game menu and in nx2navi.ini (nx2navi.ini.example lists every key). Controls: docs/controls.md.

Requirements: Windows 10 or later; an x86-64 CPU with SSE4.2 (AVX2/FMA machines get a faster build); 16 GB of RAM; about 34 GB free for the game and 1.5 GB for the launcher and its tools; a GPU with Vulkan 1.3, VK_EXT_external_memory_host and VK_EXT_mesh_shader. The setup is not signed, so SmartScreen warns on its first start.

Known issues

  • The first start after an install or update, and the first visit to an area, can pause briefly while the graphics driver builds what it has not seen; later starts are smooth.
  • Machines with 16 GB of RAM can run out of system memory in Hyrule Field.
  • Integrated AMD GPUs can fail at the title screen (their host memory heap is too small for the game's memory).
  • A rare crash in the game's particle code.

License

The source is public to read. Its additions and changes are all rights reserved (LICENSE-ADDITIONS): no part of them may be copied or published without written permission. The base import stays under its MIT License, and third-party code keeps its own license (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). No license grants anything for Nintendo's game.

NX2navi is an independent, non-commercial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. The Legend of Zelda, Ocarina of Time and Nintendo Switch are trademarks of Nintendo.

Building from source

docs/building.md lists the toolchain and the steps. tools/make_game.py also builds the game natively on Linux (docs/README-BuildKit.md, "Linux"); the launcher and the setup are Windows only. Everything the build writes stays under build\ and generated\, which git ignores, as it does the runtime's shaders the build compiles (runtime\*_spv.h; the repository holds their source only); run tools/check_content.py before a commit.

releases.name: NX2navi 0.12.0
releases.body:
NX2navi and Triforce have merged and go on as Triforce.

- This update turns NX2navi's launcher into the door to Triforce: one window that starts Triforce Setup, Triforce's
  launcher.
- Nothing of NX2navi is removed or changed: your built game, your saves and your settings stay where they are.
- **Play NX2navi** in that window still starts the game you have, for as long as you want it.
- Triforce builds the game from your own files, as NX2navi did, and its Convert saves page brings your NX2navi saves
  over.

## Good to know

- **Already have NX2navi:** the launcher updates itself to this version at its next check, as for any update. There is
  nothing to download by hand.
- **New here:** get Triforce from https://triforceproject.com. This release carries no setup.
- **What is no longer in the launcher:** its own pages for settings, mods, rebuilding the game, saves and Add to
  Steam. The game's own settings menu is unchanged.
- **Mods:** Play NX2navi starts the game as it is in its folder. A mod added after this update is not built in.
- **Steam:** a shortcut made with Add to Steam opens this window; choose Play NX2navi there.

releases.body:
**This is a preview build for testers, not a finished release.** It may have new problems. The final 0.11.0 will replace it by itself.

**How to get it:** start the launcher, open *Settings*, set *Update Channel* to **Preview**, then select *Updates*. On the Stable channel the launcher does not offer it. To go back, set the channel to Stable; the launcher keeps your previous version.

A new install uses `NX2navi-Setup-0.11.0-rc4.exe` below. The Linux AppImage is attached a few minutes after this page appears.

**The release is called 0.11.0 now.** It is the release the 0.10.2 previews were testing; no final 0.10.2 follows. The launcher offers this preview to every 0.10.2 preview.

**New since 0.10.2 preview 4:**

- Video memory staying over the card's budget once the frame rate falls under 60 fps: the textures the game has just let go of are protected for 2 seconds at any frame rate now, where it was nearly 6 seconds at 21 fps. aiSummary.oneLiner: Native x86-64 Windows recompilation of Ocarina of Time originating from Switch 2 binaries.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: NX2navi dynamically recompiles the Switch 2 version of Ocarina of Time into a standalone native application for Windows. It implements a Vulkan renderer to handle the graphics pipeline seamlessly on modern hardware. The project operates by taking user-provided game files and converting them into executable x86-64 code. This allows for native performance enhancements and resolution scaling without relying on traditional emulation overhead.
keyFeatures: Static Recompilation: Translates Switch 2 binaries directly into native Windows instructions.
Vulkan Renderer: Replaces the original graphics backend with a high-performance Vulkan pipeline.
Native Execution: Eliminates the CPU overhead typically associated with software emulators.
Asset Extraction: Builds the game natively using legally dumped user game files.
Resolution Scaling: Supports modern displays with enhanced native rendering techniques.

useCases.title: Native Gaming
useCases.description: Play Ocarina of Time on Windows PCs with optimal performance and zero emulation lag.

useCases.title: Modding Platform
useCases.description: Utilize the native architecture to create complex mods and game adjustments.

useCases.title: Graphics Enhancement
useCases.description: Render the game at modern resolutions leveraging native Vulkan APIs.

useCases.title: Preservation Research
useCases.description: Study reverse-engineering techniques applied to complex game engine binaries.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Game preservationists and enthusiasts interested in reverse engineering and native ports. Requires providing custom legally dumped game assets.
